notes:
Draw big boards fast: geometry once per change, traces in a layer

The computer example took 160 ms per frame: every frame recomputed the
pins of every part for every wire piece (own chips with their whole
pin layout) and filled every trace pixel anew. Pins, outlines, joints
and branches are now worked out once per change, the traces live in a
layer that only re-colours the wires whose signal changed, and chip
layouts, IC pin info and palette icons are kept. Now 21-28 ms per
frame, also with a clock toggling every frame; the picture is pixel
for pixel the same as before.
